classification.difficultyReason: Model repeated doubling, distinguish the initial thickness from the first fold, and convert the resulting thickness to kilometres.

content.prompt: A piece of paper $0.1$ mm thick is folded successively $100$ times. How thick is it now? Give an exact answer in millimetres and an approximation in kilometres to 3 significant figures.

answer.worked:
Each fold doubles the thickness. Including the initial thickness, the geometric sequence has $a=0.1$, $r=2$ and $101$ terms.
$$\begin{align*}a_{101}&=ar^{100}\\a_{101}&=0.1\times2^{100}\\a_{101}&=\frac{2^{100}}{10}\text{ mm}.\end{align*}$$
Since $1\text{ km}=10^6\text{ mm}$, the thickness is
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2^{100}}{10\times10^6}\text{ km}&=\frac{2^{100}}{10^7}\text{ km}\\&\approx1.27\times10^{23}\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$
